soundness_flags.label: Core Gaussian experiment and Theorems 1, 3–6
soundness_flags.one_line: The value denoted V_q(rho), its state experiment, and its claimed legal input depend essentially on w and sigma through psi and m, but q contains only conditional (A,Z) cells; replace q by a declared full index (w,q,sigma), or write V_{w,q,sigma}(rho) and quantify all theorems over it.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:known-effect-radius; Theorems 3–6
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The known shrinking radius is an abstract local-experiment restriction, not an empirically available calibration or a sampled-data confidence procedure.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The connected-saddle, certificate, profile-regret, and active-face claims are conditional results for the corrected known-radius Gaussian experiment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:uniform-iid-lift
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: No measurable observed-data interval, nuisance estimator, or Le Cam transport is yet constructed.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Any causal sampled-data coverage or expected-length claim remains conditional on a positive resolution of Open-ended Question 7.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 7 assumes a P-Donsker influence-function class, Assumptions 2–5, bounded Y, and stated nuisance-rate conditions, then gives root-n asymptotic normality; its proof is in S17.

source_verification_receipts.version: authors' revised preprint, 23 May 2003; corroborative preprint for the cited Bernoulli article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes weak-star Bayes–minimax duality for randomized confidence procedures and, for a bounded unit-variance normal mean with tau <= 2 z_(1-alpha), states that the truncated Pratt rule attains minimax expected measure.
Proposition 1 states that a uniform approximation error epsilon changes coverage probability of the approximated confidence set by at most epsilon.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corresponding to Electronic Journal of Statistics 5 (2011)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper describes the binary-tree model by polynomial equations together with positivity-induced implied inequalities, supporting the use of legal rather than merely algebraic fibers.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the Gaussian index explicit as (w,q,sigma,rho) everywhere, including the legal-input definition, active-face reduction, primal, dual, and certificate statements; then state which components are observed, externally calibrated, or fixed by design.

Add a finite worked non-singleton fiber instance with explicit w and sigma, certified numerical brackets for V, and a reproducible profile-regret gap; this would demonstrate that the curved-fiber saddle contributes beyond the inherited scalar bounded-normal reduction.

Strengthen the sampled-data lift handle into a narrower first theorem on an interior fixed-fiber submodel, with a fully specified statistic and coverage/length transfer rate before tackling topology-changing fibers and cones.

recommended_next_step: Revise the experiment indexing to include the omitted weights and outcome scales, propagate that correction through every theorem, and retain the abstract known-radius scope while developing the interior sampled-data lift as the first practical bridge.
